Award Notice - MOUTH OF THE COLUMBIA RIVER - NORTH JETTY MAJOR MAINTENANCE - PHASE II -
description: This award announcement is for the North Jetty Major Maintenance � Phase II, Klickitat County, Washington. The MCR federal navigation project is situated at the border between Washington and Oregon, where the Columbia River meets the Pacific Ocean. Deep-draft navigation through the MCR is facilitated by three primary navigation structures-North Jetty, South Jetty, and Jetty A-with a combined authorized length of 10.2 miles. The North Jetty has an authorized length of 2.5 miles extending to Station 130+00; however, it has not been constructed to its full authorized length. The initial construction of the North Jetty concluded at approximately Station 122+00, resulting in a constructed length of approximately 2.3 miles. This jetty was the second of the three to be constructed and was completed in 1917. Subsequent repairs and rehabilitations along various sections of the North Jetty were carried out in 1939, 1965, 2005, 2015, and 2019. Both initial construction and repairs utilized stone with a minimum density ranging from 167 to 180 pounds per cubic foot (pd). The side slopes of the jetty vary between 1:1.25 and 1:2 (vertical: horizontal), with an average crest elevation of 25 ft msl. Since construction, a total of 3,569,030 tons of armor stone have been placed. The Mouth of the Columbia River (MCR) North Jetty is located at the southwest corner of Washington State near Ilwaco, WA. Access to the north jetty is from N Head Rd and Cape Disappointment State Park. Mandatory work for MCR North Jetty Expedited Repairs includes toe, side slope, and crest repair construction above -5 feet NAVD88 elevation along approximately 900 feet of the jetty trunk primarily on the ocean side. These sections will be repaired and reconstructed to a design crest width of 30 feet, side slopes of 1V:2H and a crest elevation of +24.5 feet NAVD88. The estimated stone volume required for the repairs is approximately 11,100 cubic yards with an approximate minimum stone densities of 185 pounds per cubic foot. Expected stone size is between 20-40 tons each. A jetty crest haul road on top of the jetty must be constructed and staging area developed to store the large quantity of jetty armor stone.

description: SUBJECT: AOI 3 Space Intelligence � Third Call for Submissions Under the Notice ID FA8806-26-S-0001 (01 July 2026) Kronos Family of Systems (FoS) Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) 1. Purpose: This document constitutes the Third Call under the Kronos FoS CSO. Refer to the Kronos FoS CSO 2.0 for all administrative, legal, and overarching procedures. 2. This Call specifically requests Phase 1A (Quad Chart and White Paper) submissions to address Area of Interest (AOI) 3, and its Focus Area Statements (FAS) detailed below. 3. FAS #1 (AOI 03-FAS01): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks an enterprise collection management orchestration capability to coherently link existing sensor optimization and scheduling capabilities for sensing of the space domain. The capability focuses on the optimal use of finite sensors to meet collection requirements that fulfill positional tracking, operational intelligence, and foundational intelligence needs. This effort will focus not only on USSF sensors but also establish interfaces with other DoW, Intelligence Community (IC), allied, and commercial assets. A successful orchestration �brain� must demonstrate the ability to integrate multiple orchestration engines utilizing distinct scheduling paradigms (e.g., pre-planned, dynamic tip-and-cue event response, automated metric optimization), rapidly adjudicate scheduling conflicts when dynamic tasks out-prioritize deliberate needs, and disseminate commander decisions to sensors, sensor brokers, and external orchestration platforms. The capability shall consider weather, planned and unplanned outages, multiple sensor phenomenologies, tasking acknowledgment response times, PED and correlation timelines, competing prioritization schemes, and the ability to monitor execution during dynamic events. Furthermore, the proposed solution must deliver intuitive user feedback regarding collection requirement satisfaction (with full traceability), candidate rescheduling options for human review, human-in-the-loop intervention, and transparent performance metrics. A successful solution shall provide a rapid path for a prototype to host on Secret and Top Secret domains to interface with existing tasking engines and sensors. 4. FAS #2 (AOI 03-FAS02): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks innovative commercial solutions and products addressing the ability to ingest and analyze radar and sensor data for characterization of on-orbit assets. Capability should allow support analysis of radar cross sections, object discrimination and velocity and maneuver determination. 5. FAS #3 (AOI 03-FAS03): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks innovative commercial solutions and products addressing novel or innovative ways to ingest and analyze commercial RF data and distribution of data to operations centers to support object maneuver detection, status assessments, and object identification efforts. 6. FAS #4 (AOI 03-FAS04): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program seeks innovative commercial solutions and products addressing deployment of capabilities to the tactical edge, using novel or innovative methodologies to transport data back to operations centers. Solutions should demonstrate the ability to operate through disconnected connectivity and demonstrate re-sync of data once re-connected. 7. FAS #5 (AOI 3-FAS05): The SSC SYD 85 Kronos Program and its stakeholders seek innovative commercial solutions and products which enable immediate reporting of space events to the U.S. Space Command Joint Operations Center. This capability will collate all event knowledge as it�s occurring to provide Combatant Commanders, Joint Staff, and National Leadership situational awareness, real-time updates, and response options for approval. The system must be able to support both coalition space event conferences and U.S. -only space event conferences. 8. Offerors may submit more than one white paper and quad chart for this call and any future call. The white paper and quad chart proposed prototype solution may address one or more focus areas; but it must be clear in the proposed solution how the proposed prototype addresses the AOI and which focus areas. 9. Submission Timeline: Questions regarding this Call shall be submitted no later than 1200 Pacific Time on 09 September 2026. Phase 1A submissions (Quad Chart and White Paper) shall be received no later than 1700 Pacific Time on 25 September 2026. 10. Additional Information: All submission instructions, eligibility requirements, evaluation procedures, and applicable terms and conditions are contained within the Kronos FoS CSO. Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov (http://sam.gov) for amendments, answers to questions, and any updates associated with this Call. 11. title: W9127N26QA145 - PH2 BLADE SEALS REPLACEMENT for Bonneville Dam
description: GENERAL STATEMENT US Army Corps of Engineers, Portland District, Bonneville Lock and Dam are soliciting for the purchase and installation of blade seals for Powerhouse II Main Unit Kaplan turbines. The turbine runners are 5-bladed vertical axis Kaplans. The contractor will supply and install turbine blade seals on the Kaplan turbine of Main Unit 16. The second set of blade seals for Unit 17 is optional, as defined in this Performance Work Statement. The contractor will provide seals based on drawings and dimensions provided by the Government. The Government requests expedited fabrication, delivery, and installation at the earliest practicable opportunity following contract award. The Government anticipates contract award on or about 9/30/2026. This date is for planning purposes only and does not alter the Contractors performance obligations, which begin upon contract award. PERFORMANCE STANDARDS AND GUIDELINE REQUIREMENTS The Contractor shall furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, materials necessary to perform the work required under these specifications except for those items specifically identified as government provided. The Contractor shall place all trash and litter pickup in dumpsters located on the project. Telephone service will not be provided. The Contractor will furnish, deliver, and install newly manufactured Kaplan blade seals and all accessories at Bonneville Lock and Dam as detailed in this PWS. Contractor shall also provide required documentation as stated in section 5.1.3 of this PWS. Description of Supply and Service Supply Turbine Blade Seals. The Contractor is responsible for designing and fabricating one-piece solid seals for five-bladed Kaplan turbine runners. The seals are required to have redundant sealing edges, no split, and field-molded solid at site. No gluing, cold bonding, or hotbonding using additional material are permitted. The seals will need to be bonded without any external additional material (adhesive or elastomer) to ensure identical material properties across the entire seal and geometric continuity of the seal edges. title: PEO-FW Group 2 Air-Launched Effects (A2E) Assessment Event (AE)
description: PEO-FW Group 2 Air-Launched Effects (A2E) Assessment Event (AE) Submit NLT 25 September 2026 11:59 PM ET U.S. Citizens Only Purpose SOFWERX, in collaboration with the USSOCOM Program Executive Office Fixed Wing (PEO-FW), will host an Assessment Event (AE) to identify potential vendors to integrate existing compatible small, unmanned air system (sUAS) platforms into a Karman Systima Common Launch Tube (CLT). This event aims to accelerate capability insertion for platform systems to be quickly integrated into the CLT system for the purpose of launching Group 2 sUAS. Background/Synopsis The Adaptive Airborne Enterprise (A2E) is an interoperable system of systems designed to enable robust ISR capabilities through expendable, autonomous sUAS platforms, resilient data paths, and a common control architecture. FANTOM Core-enabled sUAS platforms are typically launched using the Karman Systima CLT system. Objective The objective of this assessment event is to gather information on the integration capabilities of TRL 5+ sUAS into the Karman Systima CLT for Air-Launched Effects (ALE). Specifically, the Government seeks to identify airframes capable of rapid integration into the Karman Systima Space & Defense CLT to support Find, Fix, Track, Target (F2T2) and Electronic Warfare (EW) missions under the Air Force Special Operations Command (AFSOC) A2E program. title: Market Survey � Industry Insights on Industrialized Construction (IC) Methodologies for Army Installation Resilience
description: 1. INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE This Special Notice is issued solely for market research, information, and planning purposes�it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB). There is no commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation, make awards, or pay for any costs incurred by respondents in preparing responses to this notice. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Europe District (NAU) querying the commercial marketplace to gauge industry capabilities, technical maturity, commercial availability, and execution strategies regarding Industrialized Construction (IC) and alternative construction methodologies. The objective of this market survey is to obtain strategic industry feedback to operationalize recent Department of the Army policy directives aimed at accelerating infrastructure delivery, reducing initial capital costs, and increasing real property portfolio flexibility. 2. BACKGROUND & STRATEGIC INTENT In accordance with the Department of the Army Memorandum (Facility Construction Policy Implementing Installation Resilience through Industrialized Construction (IC) Methodologies), the Army is transforming how it plans, designs, and constructs facility assets. Traditional design-bid-build processes and on-site construction methods are too slow and costly to keep pace with modem operational requirements. The intent is to accelerate the delivery of critical infrastructure, reduce initial capital costs, and increase the flexibility of the Army's real property portfolio to meet rapidly evolving warfighter requirements. Historically, Army facilities have been engineered for 50-year lifespans, often becoming functionally obsolete before structurally deficient. Moving forward, facilities will be designed to optimize an approximately 25-year lifespan. This provides strategic agility to align with supported platforms and enables rapid recapitalization by allowing structures to be repurposed or relocated as missions change. As a result, the Army seeks to transition to modern Industrialized Construction methodologies targeting: 50% faster delivery timeline compared to traditional construction. 30% reduction in initial capital costs. Optimization for an approximate 25-year facility lifespan (moving away from traditional 50-year engineering baselines) to enable strategic agility, rapid recapitalization, repurposing, or relocation as operational missions evolve. 3. TOPICS OF INTEREST: IC METHODOLOGIES & FACILITY APPLICATIONS NAU is specifically seeking industry capabilities and technical feedback regarding five (5) primary alternative construction methodologies (Ref: ASA IE&E Memo, Para 3.a�e) as applied to three (3) key facility categories (Ref: ASA IE&E Memo, Para 5.a�c), though application to other repeatable facility types is also welcomed. A. Directed Alternative Construction Methodologies (Memo Para 3.a�e) Volumetric Modular Construction: Off-site manufactured three-dimensional volumetric units transported and assembled on-site. Kit of Parts (Panelized) / Pre-Cast Systems: Prefabricated components, wall panels, and structural assemblies designed for specific building configurations. Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB): Standardized, scalable steel structural systems. Tension Fabric Structures (TFS): Rapidly deployable aluminum or steel-framed engineered fabric structures. Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing): Automated, on-site or near-site concrete/composite 3D printing systems. B. Primary Target Facility Applications (Memo Para 5.a�c) Category 1: Aircraft Hangars (Para 5.a) Primary Focus: Application of Tension Fabric Structures (TFS) providing clear-span workspaces and environmental protection, erected in a fraction of traditional construction timelines. Category 2: Maintenance Facilities (Para 5.b) Primary Focus: Application of Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB) or Panelized Steel Structures capable of supporting heavy-duty overhead cranes while standardizing procurement and accelerating erection. Category 3: Barracks, Child Development Centers (CDCs), Kennels, & Repeatable Buildings (Para 5.c) Primary Focus: Application of Volumetric Modular Construction, Kit of Parts, or Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) offering high off-site quality control, enhanced thermal performance, and rapid occupancy turnaround. 4. CORE CAPABILITY & EXPERIENCE INQUIRIES ("THE PULSE") Interested sources are requested to provide clear, concise responses to the following core inquiries: Section A: Firm Overview & Strategic Alignment General Capability: Briefly describe your firm�s primary business model, technical focus, manufacturing capacity (if applicable), and experience operating as a prime contractor or key technology partner in Industrialized Construction. Target Scope & Capacity: What is your firm�s ideal project scale (e.g., square footage, dollar value, or unit volume per year) for delivering IC solutions? Section B: Technical Evaluation of Methodologies (Memo 3.a�e vs 5.a�c) Methodology Alignment: Detail your firm�s specific capabilities and execution track record in one or more of the following: -Volumetric Modular -Kit of Parts / Panelized Pre-Cast -Pre-Engineered Metal Buildings (PEMB) -Tension Fabric Structures (TFS) -Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing) Facility Application & Suitability: How well do your IC methodologies integrate with the designated facility types (Hangars, Maintenance Shops, Barracks/CDCs/Repeatable Structures)? What technical modifications or building code considerations are critical for DoD adoption? Are there other facility types that are not included in this announcement that your firm believes would be good candidates for IC methodologies? 25-Year Lifespan & Flexibility Optimization: With the Department of War�s stated objective of reducing the expected lifespan of these facilities to be constructed from 50 years to 25 years in order to achieve lower investment and maintenance costs, do you believe that the IC construction methodologies contemplated by this memorandum are viable delivery methods to meet the 25 year life span expectation? How do the IC methodology capabilities that your company possesses a 25-year optimized lifecycle? Discuss disassembly, relocation, structural repurposing, and recapitalization advantages of your system compared to traditional 50-year brick-and-mortar builds. Section C: Cost, Schedule, & Delivery Optimization Speed & Cost Metrics: How can your firm achieve or approach the Army's benchmark goals of 50% faster delivery and a 30% cost reduction? Supply Chain & Logistics: What are the key supply chain, manufacturing lead time, or transportation constraints associated with scaling your IC methodology across domestic (CONUS) and/or overseas (OCONUS) military installations? Contracting & Delivery Models: What project delivery models best support your manufacturing and installation workflows? Section D: Sourced Experience & Project History Provide up to three (3) representative project examples completed within the past five (5) years demonstrating successful implementation of IC methodologies. For each project, specify: Facility type and delivery methodology utilized (from Para 3.a�e). Timeline comparison (design/fabrication/erection time vs traditional estimated baseline). Cost performance and life-cycle/re-use features. Key lessons learned and recommendations for Government adoption. 5. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS Firms possessing the capability, experience, and interest in supporting the Army's Industrialized Construction policy are invited to submit their responses in accordance with the following parameters: Response Parameters: Page Limit: Not to exceed ten (10) pages total (including cover page and attachments). Format: Microsoft Word (.docx) or Adobe PDF (.pdf) format, standard 12-pt font. Submittal Address: Submissions must be sent electronically via email to: Primary POC: andrew.a.cochran@usace.army.mil Secondary POC: ryan.s.shoemake

description: On August 28, 2026, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Technology Acquisition Center, located at 23 Christopher Way, Eatontown, NJ 07724 issued Firm-Fixed Price Delivery Order NNG15SD38B 36C10B25F0303 to RedHawk IT Solutions, LLC under the terms and conditions of its National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP) V Government-Wide Acquisition Contract, NNG15SD38B, and modifications thereto. The action was solicited on a brand name basis as a Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business set-aside as the result of Market Research. Through this action, VA procured Brand Name Plum Laboratories, Inc. Plum Case Retrofit to retrofit and upgrade existing brand name Plum Enterprise ENT Cases (quantity of 165- Part Number ENT0007) with brand name services and components. Upon completion, the cases will meet the same specification as Plum Enterprise SR Mini with PCX (Star-link ready) (Part Number ENTSR0002). Also included in this requirement is an Optional Task for an additional (1) year of Brand Name Enterprise Network Cloud Management (NCM) license for each Plum Case upgraded, which shall co-term with the overarching footprint of licenses. The contract is issued with one (1) 12-Month base period and one (1) 12-Month period for the Optional task. The base Period of Performance (PoP) for the Plum Case Retrofit effort shall be from August 28, 2026 through August 27, 2027. The Optional Task for each case shall begin upon completion of the retrofit upgrade and shall co-term with the overarching VA NetCloud management licenses. The ultimate contract completion date, inclusive of the Optional Task, is August 27, 2028. In accordance with RFO 16.507-6(f)(1), the award notice for this action will be synopsized on the Contract Opportunities website and this justification will be made publicly available within 14 days of award
